The cap is how many launches Stage 2 PLANS; the floor is how many it must SCORE. So cap minus floor is the number of planned launches a candidate may LOSE and still reach a verdict at all — to a request-cap drop, to a create slot the co-ordination rule marks nothing in (measure.mjs -> roomIsProven, decision 134a), to a window too young or unwalkable, or to any mix of them. At 10 a candidate absorbs TWO. Until 190a this value was 8, EQUAL to the floor, which absorbed NONE: one dropped launch left 7 scored and scoreEntry returned entry-unmeasured for the WHOLE CANDIDATE. That equality was never a decision — it was the coincidence of two separately-argued numbers, and nothing failed when it started costing verdicts. WHY TWO AND NOT ONE, which is the only real question here. The per-launch drop rate is MEASURED, not assumed: at the 85,000ms reach this file pins, 4 of the 127 committed launches that can show the effect exceed what maxRequestsPerLaunch affords and are dropped whole — 3.1% (seekMarginMs owns that measurement and its population). Treating a candidate's planned launches as independent draws at THAT CAUSE ALONE, the chance of finishing SHORT of the floor is 22.6% at zero spare launches, 3.1% at one, and 0.32% at two. One spare launch is therefore not enough on its own, and the independence assumption is where it fails WORST: cap-hit drops are a property of how busy a launch is, and busy launches cluster on busy deployers, so a candidate that drops one is more likely than the base rate to drop a second — and those candidates are exactly the most gate-relevant ones. Two spare launches is the cheapest gap that survives that correlation rather than assuming it away. THOSE THREE FIGURES ARE THE REQUEST-CAP COMPONENT ONLY, AND NOBODY MAY READ 0.32% AS THE FULL-DAY RUN'S EXPECTED NO-VERDICT RATE. They are computed from the 4-in-127 page-cost drop rate and from nothing else. The DOMINANT cause for a stranger is the other one named above, and this repository already measures it: census/2026-08-03-bundling-census.md reads per-launch proven at 44 of 112 = 0.3929 under the union predicate, and 0 of 13 STRANGERS proven on all eight (1 of 14 counting our own control, which is the one). At about 39% proven per launch, 8-of-10 proven is not reachable for a typical stranger, so the full-day run's no-verdict rate will be governed by roomIsProven and NOT by the 0.32% pinned here. The other half of that is honest too: this cap raise DOES help the dominant cause, since the same census recorded 3 candidates sitting at 7 of 8 that a two-launch gap now reaches — but this lane does not quantify that, and the pinned figure must not be read as if it did. THE FLOOR IS NOT THE ADJUSTABLE HALF: closing this gap by lowering minLaunchesSampled would weaken the evidence a verdict rests on rather than give it headroom, and 190a names the direction explicitly. NO BAR MOVED and no launch is scored on weaker terms — every scored launch clears exactly what it cleared at 8, and the only change is that the walk is offered two more of them, reaching two launches further back in a candidate's history. COST, STATED HERE RATHER THAN DISCOVERED LATER. The stage arithmetic goes 3 x 8 x 18 = 432 to 3 x 10 x 18 = 540 requests, a 25% rise carried entirely by maxKeylessRequests, which moved with it so the ceiling and the declared worst case are still the SAME number. Wall clock at the pinned 7s swap-api pacing, AT THE SCORING CAP OF 3 THIS DECISION WAS TAKEN AT: about 63 minutes worst case against about 50 before, and about 21 minutes typical against about 17 at the measured ~6 requests a launch. At the scoring cap of 7 pinned on 2026-08-04 the same arithmetic reads about 147 and about 49. It spends NO keyed request and no vendor allowance at any size. The COST LEG's separate exposure is re-derived and ITS CEILING MOVED WITH THIS CAP (captain decision 197b): entryCostTargets over the committed tape reads p50 19 / p90 35 / p95 41 / max 74 distinct transactions per launch, so at 10 launches a candidate costs about 190 at the median and about 350 at p90, and stage2_cost.maxRpcRequestsPerCandidate went 400 -> 500 to hold the PER-LAUNCH headroom at 50 union transactions rather than let this cap cut it to 40 — 500 / 10 = 400 / 8. The median and the p90 fit inside 400 as well; what the raise consumed is the margin ABOVE them, and a launch the ceiling cannot cover is skipped WHOLE, which pushes minPricedFraction 0.8 towards entry-cost-unmeasured on exactly the busiest candidates. That entry owns the arithmetic and the measured margins. bundling_census reads this cap rather than re-pinning it, so its own derived ceiling moved 4,320 to 5,400 for the same reason. STAGE 0 WAS RE-RUN AT THIS VALUE and still refuses the known-negative control: subjectEntryRecent reads entry-room-absent over the last 10 launches, and the rolling replay reads 226 windows, 92 present, 134 absent, 0 unmeasured and 0 false positives. A CEILING THIS LANE DOES NOT CLOSE: DECOUPLING THE CAP FROM THE FLOOR CREATES A VERDICT SHAPE THAT WAS STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE AT 8-AND-8. A candidate may now be scored on 8 of 10 launches whose 2 missing launches were selected BY DROP CAUSE rather than at random - request-cap drops fall on the busiest launches, roomIsProven drops on launches with no co-ordination evidence. At 8-and-8 such a candidate returned entry-unmeasured; it now returns a verdict computed over a non-random subsample. This is the same shape the repo elsewhere refuses to read at all: the cost leg discards a ceiling-truncated launch WHOLE because a truncated walk holds the earliest entrants by slot and is a biased sample rather than a short one, and minPricedFraction exists for the same reason. THE DIRECTION OF THAT BIAS IS UNMEASURED, and the attempt that failed to settle it is the evidence rather than a hand-wave: over the 235 committed launches the rank correlation between per-launch fill count and roomLeft is 0.0250, i.e. negligible; the busiest quartile's median roomLeft is 0.3032 against the quietest quartile's 0.2771, which points one way; but dropping the busiest 7 of 235 (the 3.1% request-cap rate) moves the median roomLeft 0.3146 -> 0.3314, i.e. UP, TOWARD 'enterable', which points the other way. Two statistics, OPPOSITE IN SIGN, on n = 1 deployer: the direction is not established. What it does and does not imply: on this tape it changes no verdict, because the median roomLeft of 0.3146 sits 0.24 BELOW the minRoomLeft bar of 0.55 - but that is n = 1 and says nothing about a stranger sitting near the bar. So the standing bar ('a null result is an acceptable result, a false positive is not') is NOT DISCHARGED for this new sample shape by this lane. Captain decision 198b accepted that knowingly and split the work: a refuse-near-the-bar guard is a SEPARATE FILED LANE blocked on this one, and the full-day screen run blocks on BOTH, so the unguarded verdict shape is never what that run uses. THE REQUEST-CAP UNMEASURED RATE THIS GAP BUYS IS PINNED BY A TEST, not left implicit — test/deployer-screen.test.ts, 'THE SAMPLING RULE HAS HEADROOM, and the REQUEST-CAP unmeasured rate it buys is PINNED' — so neither this value nor minLaunchesSampled can move THAT COMPONENT silently again. It is the component and never the total: what the full-day run answers nothing at will be governed by roomIsProven, which no test here pins.
justification.maxRequestsPerLaunch: MEASURED from the committed tape's own build metadata, and the POPULATION MATTERS because the tape's windows are not all the same length. A live Stage 2 walk always reads a 60s window, and over the 210 committed launches whose stored window_ms is 60000 the pages needed per launch run p50 4, p90 6, p95 6, MAX 13. The pooled figure across all 235 covered launches — p50 4, p90 8, p95 13, MAX 24 — is inflated by the 21 of them taped over 300s (and 4 over 120s), and it is what an earlier version of this entry quoted. The cap is on REQUESTS rather than pages because the endpoint sheds ~24.7% of what it is asked for (51,715 OK against 16,960 HTTP 429 on that same build) and the client retries; counting only successes would let a launch cost 3x the printed plan. At that shed rate a page costs ~1.33 requests, and a page is only STARTED when a whole 3-request page cost still fits (i.e. at spent <= 15), so 18 requests starts ABOUT 11-12 PAGES — not the 13-14 an earlier version claimed, which counted requests the loop will not spend. WHAT THAT COVERS, STATED EXACTLY RATHER THAN ROUNDED UP: 11-12 pages is roughly double the 60s p95 of 6, but it does NOT cover that population's observed maximum of 13 — the 2 launches in 210 (1.0%) that needed 13 pages would be dropped at the mean shed rate. That is the reported failure below, not a silent one, and it is why the value does not move: raising the cap to cover a 1% tail costs the whole 7 x 10 x 18 = 1,260 stage arithmetic (3 x 8 x 18 = 432 before captain decision 190a raised the launch cap, and 3 x 10 x 18 = 540 before the proof-coverage lane raised the scoring cap to 7 on 2026-08-04), and it is under open captain decision 193c besides. THE BOUND IS EXACT RATHER THAN APPROXIMATE: a page can cost up to 3 requests (one attempt plus two backoffs), so the walk reserves the WHOLE per-page cost before starting a page and a launch therefore costs at most 18 and never 20. Checking the cap only between pages would have let a walk with one request of headroom spend three, breaking the stage arithmetic the dry run prints as the entire exposure. THE TAIL IS DROPPED, NOT TRUNCATED SILENTLY: a launch that spends the cap without reaching the mint is reported as DROPPED with its own note, and the sampling bias is stated because the launches too busy to walk are exactly the interesting ones.
justification.keylessMinIntervalMs: GOVERNS ONE HOST: swap-api.pump.fun, the fill walk, and only it. `budget.keylessMinIntervalMs` stays at 2000ms for frontend-api-v3, which has shed nothing here and must not be slowed for a fault on a different host. 7000ms is anchored on TWO INDEPENDENT READINGS OF THIS HOST. (i) LIVE: at 2000ms two consecutive Stage 2 runs against swap-api each lost 4 of the subject's 8 launches to HTTP 429 after all three attempts, so the run reported `entry-unmeasured` where the truth is `entry-room-absent`; the same code at 7000ms walked all 8 and produced `entry-room-absent`. A fast wrong answer is worth nothing, and the failure is silent in the direction that matters — a dropped launch degrades the verdict rather than announcing the pacing is wrong. (ii) THE TAPE BUILDER'S OWN RECORD against this same endpoint: the committed `window/*.meta.json` `delay` field — the adaptive delay each build settled on — reads p50 4.92s, p75 15s, p90 15.5s, max 40s, with only p10-p25 near 1.2s; and its shed share by delay quartile is 24.2% / 24.8% / 28.5% / 23.8% over the 238 builds carrying a stats block, i.e. 23.8-28.5% with the SLOWEST quartile no better than the fastest — an earlier version of this entry called that 'flat at ~24-25%', which understates the third quartile by ~4 points without changing what it establishes: backing off does not buy immunity and there is no cheap corner to sit in. 7s is therefore pinned deliberately between that p50 and p75 rather than at the bottom of the range. COST: the request arithmetic is untouched BY THIS PIN — pacing moves wall clock and never exposure — but the wall clock is not, so at the launch cap of 10 captain decision 190a set and the scoring cap of 7 the proof-coverage lane set (7 x 10 x 18 = 1,260) the typical run is about 49 minutes and the worst case about 147, and every printed estimate says so. At the launch cap of 8 this entry was written against the same pacing read about 17 and about 50, and at a scoring cap of 3 against a launch cap of 10 it read about 21 and about 63.
justification.keylessRetryBackoffMs: The tape build shed a quarter of its requests and its own recorded delay ranges from 0.75s to 40s, i.e. it backed off and retried through them. A client that treats a 429 as terminal cannot walk this endpoint at all - the first live check of the pager died on one, three launches in. Two retries at 3s and 9s clear the ordinary case, and EVERY attempt counts against both the per-launch cap and the stage ceiling, so a retry-heavy run gets a dropped launch rather than an unbounded one.
justification.tradePageLimit: 100 is what the trade endpoint serves per page and is the figure the AGENTS.md note is anchored on. Asking for less would multiply the request count for no benefit; the endpoint's own cap is what it is.
justification.windowMs: 60000 is the window_ms of 210 of the committed population tape's 239 launches — its MODAL window and not its only one: 25 were taped over 300000 and 4 over 120000, and calling it 'the tape's window_ms' (as an earlier version of this entry did) hides the 5x builds that inflate every page distribution measured across the whole tape (see maxRequestsPerLaunch). It has NO live use of its own any more: it is a FLOOR inside pumpfun.mjs -> windowReachMs, and nothing else reads it. That one derivation answers BOTH forward-reaching questions ON THE SWAP-API SOURCE — how far the seek cursor must reach past the mint, and whether a launch is old enough to have finished happening — because there they are the same instant. SCOPED RATHER THAN WEAKENED, AND THE SCOPE IS THE CORRECTION: this entry used to state it of Stage 2 flatly, and captain decision 260a's fill-source injection makes eligibility a question asked of the fill source, so 'both questions, one function' is a property of the swap-api source and not of Stage 2 in general. The swap-api derivation and every figure below it are untouched. It does NOT decide which fills are inside the measured window — windowSlotSpan does — because the mint time it would be measured from comes from the vendor and the fills come from pump.fun, and there is nothing to reconcile the two clocks with. HISTORY, read the tense, because this value has been mis-scoped TWICE and the second time is the instructive one. It once decided eligibility alone, so a launch aged 60-65s passed 'old enough to have finished happening' while the newest instant the walk reaches for had not happened yet — the same tail truncation seekMarginMs exists to prevent, arriving from the future side. The fix was the hand-written sum windowMs + seekMarginMs = 65000ms, which was correct only while the seek cursor was ALSO 65000ms and the 160-slot span was reckoned at a nominal 400ms/slot (64.0s). Captain decision 144a moved the cursor to windowReachMs and left that sum behind, and the chain then drifted past the nominal rate unaided: at the measured 446.55ms/slot maximum 160 slots is 71448ms, so the sum ran 6448ms short of the span and 20000ms short of the reach, and a launch could be admitted 20s before the cursor's own bound was in the past. RAISING THE SUM TO 71448 WOULD HAVE RE-ARMED THE IDENTICAL TRAP, because the defect was never the number — it was writing a DURATION for something the chain controls. Both questions derive from windowSlotSpan at a MEASURED worst-case slot rate through the one function, on that source. That rate is a PINNED constant, so the gate moves only when the slot rate is re-measured against a newer committed tape and the pin is raised — what the derivation buys is that a chain slowing past the pin fails the tape-derived guard loudly instead of silently leaving the gate short, and that raising the pin moves the gate and the seek cursor together. Membership stays windowSlotSpan's alone regardless. The old assertion windowSlotSpan x 400ms <= windowMs + seekMarginMs no longer exists — it was denominated in the variable that did not move, so it stayed true and went out of validity with nothing failing. Coverage is now enforced by the describe block 'the seek cursor reaches the whole declared slot window, at a MEASURED slot rate' in test/deployer-screen.test.ts, which re-derives the slot rate from the committed tapes on every run, asserts the reach covers the whole declared span, and asserts the eligibility gate IS that reach — read out of a live scoreCandidateEntry rather than off the source text. Widening the span still fails loudly, through that block.
justification.windowSlotSpan: MEASURED, and deliberately NOT ceil(windowMs/400)=150, which is measurably too narrow. Across the 210 committed launches whose stored window_ms is 60000 the observed slot span is p50 151, p75 153, p90 155, p95 155, MAX 158 — and 51% of them hold at least one fill beyond createSlot+150 (37.1% beyond 151, 5.2% beyond 155, 0.0% beyond 160). This is not a rounding nuisance: the trailing fills are disproportionately LATE SELLS, and dropping one flips a wallet from closed to open, which shrinks fieldClosedRoundTrips — itself a gate at minFieldRoundTrips 10. So a too-narrow span silently changes gate outcomes. 160 covers 100% of observed windows with margin over the observed max of 158. THE OTHER DIRECTION, ON THE RECORD RATHER THAN AS AN OBJECTION: at the tape's observed rate (60s <-> p50 151 slots, ~397ms/slot) 160 slots is ~63.5s, so the live window is up to ~3.5s WIDER than the tape's 60s windows, and the extra late sells make realised P&L read better than the ground-truth recipe would. Because the field leg is veto-only it loosens rather than tightens — a too-generous field can only fail to veto, never earn a verdict — and the magnitude is small. THAT MAGNITUDE CLAIM IS CITED, NOT MEASURED HERE: the figure behind it (the margin sits at the thinnest part of the window, p50 18 / p95 52 fills in the last 5s) is carried over from the PR #7 review comment that recorded this tradeoff, which supplied it without naming a population, and it is reproduced nowhere in this repo — unlike the span figures above, which name theirs (the 210 committed launches whose stored window_ms is 60000). 160 was chosen on measurement, so no change is implied. WHICH OF THE TWO CONVERSIONS OF 160 SLOTS TO READ: the ~63.5s above is the TAPE'S OWN OBSERVED RATE (~397ms/slot, from 60s <-> p50 151 slots) and is SUPERSEDED by the 71448ms figure below, which converts the same 160 slots at the MEASURED WORST-CASE 446.55ms/slot. Both describe the same span and differ only in the rate; the chain's rate rose between them. Re-deriving the ~63.5s conversion and the ~3.5s-wider claim resting on it belongs to A SEPARATE LANE, so the older number is left standing rather than silently updated — read it as history, and read 71448ms as the bound anything in force is measured against. NOTE THE INTERACTION WITH ELIGIBILITY: this span is what decides a launch is old enough to measure, through pumpfun.mjs -> windowReachMs and no other route. HISTORY, and it is worth the tense, because the same claim failed twice here. This entry used to say the eligibility gate DOMINATED the span (160 slots being 64.0s at the nominal 400ms/slot against a 65000ms gate) and that a test pinned windowSlotSpan x 400ms <= windowMs + seekMarginMs. That inequality was DELETED because it was denominated in the variable that did not move: the span never changed, the chain's slot rate did, so it stayed true and went out of validity with nothing failing. Captain decision 144a then scaled the SEEK CURSOR with this span while the eligibility gate stayed a hand-written 65000ms, i.e. 6448ms short of the 71448ms this span is worth at the measured 446.55 ms/slot maximum and 20000ms short of the reach. Both halves now derive from this span at that measured rate, so widening the span widens the reach AND the gate together and neither can outrun it. The enforcement is the describe block 'the seek cursor reaches the whole declared slot window, at a MEASURED slot rate' in test/deployer-screen.test.ts, which re-derives the slot rate from the committed tapes on every run, asserts the reach covers the whole declared span, and asserts the eligibility gate IS that reach. Widening the span still fails loudly, through that block. STAGE 0 DELIBERATELY DOES NOT USE THIS: it measures each committed launch over its own stored window, because the 1,502-pair reproduction against wallet_launch_pnl.csv is computed that way and that regression guard is not traded for cosmetic consistency between the two paths.
justification.seekMarginMs: The walk seeks from createdAtMs + windowReachMs = max(windowMs, ceil(windowSlotSpan x MAX_MS_PER_SLOT)) + this, i.e. 85000ms at the pinned values: a reach derived from the SPAN at a measured worst-case slot rate (MEASURED_MAX_MS_PER_SLOT 446.55 x SLOT_RATE_MARGIN 1.1 -> MAX_MS_PER_SLOT 500), with windowMs surviving there only as a FLOOR. HISTORY: before captain decision 144a the seek was createdAtMs + windowMs + this, and this margin placed the cursor; it no longer does. This margin is added ON TOP of that span-derived reach and keeps its own separate job — clock slack, so a vendor mint time running EARLY by less than 5s cannot cut the tail off the window before the slot trim ever sees it. It replaces a tail-truncation detector that could not discriminate — launches simply stop trading before the nominal window end (p50 observed span 151 against a 160 span), so any such detector fires on nearly every launch and carries no information. Designing the failure out beats reporting it. COST: the walk still pages BACKWARDS to the mint and still trims by slot afterwards, so the margin only adds rows at the newest end — about 5s of trading, roughly 30 fills at a p50 of 362 fills per window over the 210 launches taped at 60s — the population a live walk matches; pooled across all 235 covered launches the p50 is 381 and the answer is the same — i.e. at most one extra page of 100. THAT PARAGRAPH SIZES THE MARGIN ALONE AND IS NO LONGER THE WALK'S COST, which is the span-derived reach's: at 85000ms rather than 65000ms the page cost over the 127 committed launches that can show the effect goes p50 5 / p90 7 / p95 8 / max 14 to p50 6 / p90 8 / p95 9 / max 17, and 4 of 127 = 3.1% now exceed the ~16 pages maxRequestsPerLaunch affords and are dropped as request-cap, where it was 0 of 127. (That is its own measurement over its own named population and is NOT the '1% tail' maxRequestsPerLaunch cites, which is 2 launches in 210 over the 60s-taped population that structurally cannot show this gap. Do not read the two as the same number. pumpfun.mjs -> windowReachMs owns the whole page-cost story and test/deployer-screen.test.ts pins these same figures.) THE CONSEQUENCE IS THE CANDIDATE'S, NOT THE LAUNCH'S, AND THE ZERO-SLACK HALF OF IT IS NOW FIXED (captain decision 190a). When this entry was written minLaunchesSampled and maxLaunchesPerCandidate were the same pinned value (8), so there was no slack — ONE such drop among a candidate's 8 planned launches left 7 sampled and scoreEntry returned entry-unmeasured for the WHOLE CANDIDATE, a naive independent-launches ESTIMATE of 1 - (1 - 4/127)^8 = about 22.6% of candidates. The cap is now 10 against the same floor of 8, so a candidate absorbs TWO drops and the same estimate falls to about 0.32%; maxLaunchesPerCandidate owns that arithmetic and its correlation caveat, and a test pins the figure. The DROP RATE ITSELF IS UNCHANGED — this margin still costs 4 of 127 launches, and that is the number this entry is responsible for. Both estimates take their base rate from ONE deployer's long-window launches, which are also the busiest on the tape. An unmeasured verdict is 'no answer' and never a rejection, and the drop is counted and reported where the truncated tail was silent. The stage arithmetic moved with the caps and not with this margin: 7 x 10 x 18 = 1,260, where it was 3 x 10 x 18 = 540 before the scoring cap went to 7 and 3 x 8 x 18 = 432 before the launch cap went to 10. IT ALSO BOUNDS ELIGIBILITY, because it must, AND THAT IS THE SAME BOUND RATHER THAN A SECOND ONE: a launch is not old enough to measure until the instant the seek cursor reaches for is in the past, so on the swap-api walk the gate IS the reach — 85000ms at the pinned values — and moves with it. NO MODULE AND FUNCTION NAME IS GIVEN FOR THAT GATE ANY MORE, AND THE DELETION IS THE CORRECTION. This entry used to say 'stage2.mjs and bundling.mjs both skip a launch younger than windowReachMs — the identical call'. Captain decision 260a's Stage 2 fill-source injection moves that call: eligibility becomes a question asked of whichever fill source Stage 2 was given, and windowReachMs is what the SWAP-API source answers it with rather than what those two modules call. THE DERIVATION THIS ENTRY OWNS IS UNCHANGED and so is the 85000ms it produces; what changed is that a call site is not a durable anchor for it. A justification anchored on one goes stale with nothing failing — the same defect shape as the windowSlotSpan x 400ms inequality this file records deleting, which stayed true while ceasing to mean anything. What guarantees the gate IS the reach is the test named below, read out of a live scoreCandidateEntry, and that is the thing to check. A launch has finished happening exactly when the instant the cursor seeks to is in the past, so there is nothing left to reconcile. HISTORY: the gate was a hand-written windowMs + seekMarginMs = 65000ms, which held only while the cursor was also 65000ms; captain decision 144a moved the cursor and the chain kept drifting, leaving the gate 6448ms short of the 71448ms the 160-slot span is worth at the measured 446.55 ms/slot maximum and 20000ms short of the reach. It shipped as a knowing residual because the error is one-directional and safe — an early-admitted launch loses its late sells, so its field reads WORSE, and the field leg is veto-only — but it is the class of false rejection that is permanent and invisible, since a graded wallet is filed and never offered again. Raising the constant to 71448 would have re-armed the trap at the next drift; deriving it removes the class. The gate is now asserted, from a live scoreCandidateEntry, by the test 'THE ELIGIBILITY GATE IS THE SAME BOUND, derived' in test/deployer-screen.test.ts. THIS IS A CURSOR HINT AND NOT A TOLERANCE: the pre-mint tripwire still compares ts < createdAtMs with ZERO slack (the measured gap is exactly 0 on all 235 committed launches) and coverage is still discharged only by the endpoint explicitly saying nothing older exists.
justification.maxKeylessRequests: Stage 2's own sub-ceiling, enforced on its own client so it cannot eat the --consistency pass's budget. 7 x 10 x 18 = 1,260 is the exact declared worst case, so no plan-level truncation is possible: the ceiling and the plan agree, and the dry run prints both. It was 432 at a launch cap of 8 and 540 at a scoring cap of 3; captain decision 190a raised the launch cap to 10 for headroom against a dropped launch and the proof-coverage lane raised the scoring cap to 7 on 2026-08-04, and this ceiling moved WITH each of them, because the two being the same number is the property that makes the dry run the whole exposure. Typical cost is far lower - at the measured p50 of 4 pages plus shedding it is about 6 requests a launch, so roughly 420 for a full run. At the pinned 7s pacing for this host that is about 49 minutes typical against about 147 minutes worst case, and the run prints both so an operator does not mistake a slow walk for a hang. A launch is only started when a full per-launch cap of headroom remains, so a run can never abandon a launch half-walked.

$comment: NOT LIVE, AND THAT IS THE CORRECT RESTING STATE, stated first rather than buried. The captain's
Dune-aggregated Stage 2 programme cuts over at Gate 3, which has not been convened; screen.mjs
selects the swap-api fill source on every run, so no run has ever read a number in this block and
no execution has ever been billed at these caps. Everything here is arithmetic over measurements
already taken. Read that as this block's largest limit.
WHY IT EXISTS. The three caps below are the SAME three the swap-api source carries in
stage2_entry, and until now there was one set shared by both. That could not survive the
substitution, because the two sources do not cost the same thing: the swap-api walk spends
REQUESTS, a page at a time, per launch; this source spends CREDITS on one batched execution and
pays for how much of the decoded trade tables it must SCAN. One shared set would have to be
justified by one source's arithmetic and obeyed by both — and on the other source the value that
arithmetic produced would be CARRIED, not derived, which is the defect this block was written to
remove. The captain's ruling (2026-08-05, relayed to this lane) is that each source carries its
own three, each justified by its own cost model, and that neither justification may describe
arithmetic the other source obeys. test/deployer-screen.test.ts asserts that separation.
THIS BLOCK IS THE THREE SAMPLING CAPS AND NOTHING ELSE. Every EVIDENCE bar — minRoomLeft, the
field bars, maxEntryCostPerSolStaked, minPricedFraction — is a property of the QUESTION and not
of the transport, so it stays in stage2_entry and governs both sources unchanged. A source that
carried its own minRoomLeft could be made to answer differently about the same window, which is
the one thing the substitution must never be able to do.
THE COST MODEL AND ITS PROVENANCE. Gate 1 measured the entry statement at roughly 29 CREDITS PER
RUN at the bars in force — maxCandidatesScored 7 x maxLaunchesPerCandidate 10 = 70 launch windows
scanned — returning 240 datapoints per candidate, i.e. 10 rows of 24 columns, one row per planned
launch. THOSE MEASUREMENTS ARE HELD IN FIRSTMATE'S RECORDS AND NOT IN THIS REPO, so they are
asserted from elsewhere and no test here can check them. The arithmetic BUILT on them below is
checkable and is checked.
THE LEVER IS WINDOWS SCANNED, NOT ROWS RETURNED. Rows returned are candidates x launches — 154 at
the caps below, against the 40,000 of dune.maxResultRows, two orders of magnitude of headroom —
and 528 datapoints a candidate at 24 columns, against 240 at the measured bars. Neither binds
anything. What the execution is billed for is the SCAN, which scales with the number of launch
windows the statement must cover. So the caps below are derived from windows scanned, and the row
ceiling is left to do the job it already does: refuse a result that cannot prove it is whole.

justification.maxCandidatesScored: 7, and on THIS source it is a CREDIT bound. WHAT FIXES IT: windows scanned is the lever, a candidate is maxLaunchesPerCandidate 22 windows, and 7 candidates is 154 windows — about 64 credits a run at the ~0.414 credits a window the block comment derives (roughly 29 credits over the 70 windows Gate 1 measured, held in firstmate's records and not in this repo). THE CEILING IT FITS UNDER: the Dune free tier is 2,500 credits a MONTH and SHARED across every lane in this repo (see the dune block), so ~64 a run is ~39 full runs a month before the enumeration and census lanes take their own share of the same allowance — a real ceiling, which is what makes this a bound rather than a number too large to bite. THE MATCHING INTEGER IS NOT CONTINUITY AND MUST NOT BE READ AS IT: stage2_entry.maxCandidatesScored is also 7 and is fixed by a request product that has no meaning here, while this 7 is fixed by a credit budget that has no meaning there. Neither derivation may be read across. THE CAP IS KNOWN TO BE COSTING COVERAGE AND THIS BLOCK DOES NOT FIX THAT — captain decision 266c, which is why the parameter was re-derived rather than carried. On the 2026-08-05 tiered seed comparison the cap BOUND for the first time: 13 of leg B's 27 gate survivors went unscored for cap reasons alone (7 of 14 on good, 6 of 13 on elite). That one is checkable in this repo — runs/2026-08-05-seed-comparison.md and the three records under measurements/2026-08-05-seed-comparison/, whose scoringCap blocks carry the counts. It is a cap and not a refusal, and scoringCap.survivorsUnscored is where a run says so. WHAT RAISING IT WOULD COST, so the next decision has a number rather than an argument: credits scale with windows, so 14 candidates is 308 windows and ~128 credits a run (~19 runs a month), and 27 — the survivor count that actually went unserved — is 594 windows and ~246 credits, ~10 runs a month. WHAT STILL CANNOT FIX IT is the survivor count itself: the committed runs disagree about the gate-pass rate by nearly an order of magnitude (4 of 82 against 5 of 12), so at budget.maxCandidates 195 the survivor count spans about 10 to about 81 and no cap derived from that range means anything. Raising this value is a captain decision with a credit price attached, not an inference from a survivor count.
justification.minLaunchesSampled: 20, and THE ANCHOR IS EVIDENCE RATHER THAN BUDGET — which is the whole difference between this block and stage2_entry, where the same parameter is 8 and says plainly that it is a budget bound. The smallest per-launch bucket the June report was willing to state a quartile spread over is era B at n = 20 (slot-zero-june-regime-change 6.2, 'Per-launch non-cohort create-slot return per SOL, distribution across launches', held in firstmate's records and not in this repo). 20 IS THAT NUMBER AND NO OTHER: it is the only raise this project has evidence for, and inventing a different one would be the defect this block exists to remove. WHAT MADE IT REACHABLE HERE IS THE COST MODEL AND NOTHING ABOUT THE EVIDENCE, which never changed. On the swap-api source a floor of 20 needs a cap of 22 and that source's own request ceiling does not afford it — its entry owns that arithmetic and keeps 8. Here a launch costs a scanned window, so a floor of 20 at a cap of 22 costs ~64 credits a run and fits. The bar did not move because the evidence improved; it moved because a cheaper transport let this source afford the sample the evidence always wanted. THE CONSEQUENCE, STATED BECAUSE IT IS UNCOMFORTABLE AND RUNS AGAINST THIS BLOCK: raising the floor makes a verdict HARDER to reach, not easier. A candidate must now have 20 of 22 planned launches SCORED, and the dominant hole is not budget but measure.mjs -> roomIsProven, which the bundling census reads at 44 of 112 = 0.3929 proven per launch under the union predicate and 0 of 13 strangers proven on all eight (census/2026-08-03-bundling-census.md). At about 39% proven per launch, 8-of-10 was already out of reach for a typical stranger and 20-of-22 is further out of it. So this floor should be expected to RAISE the entry-unmeasured rate on strangers, and an unmeasured verdict is no answer rather than a rejection — carried forward and counted, never dropped (captain decision 174b). Nothing here touches roomIsProven, and no measurement in this repo says how much further out of reach 20-of-22 puts it; that is unquantified and is the first thing a Gate 3 run should report. THE SECOND CONSEQUENCE: the same wallet scored through the two sources rests its verdict on different sample sizes — at least 20 launches here, at least 8 there — so the two are not interchangeable evidence about one deployer, and a reader must check the record's entry.launchesSampled before pooling them. THE FLOOR IS STILL NOT THE ADJUSTABLE HALF: it stays below maxLaunchesPerCandidate so a dropped launch costs a launch rather than the candidate's whole verdict, and lowering it to buy headroom would weaken the evidence a verdict rests on — the direction captain decision 190a named and refused.
justification.maxLaunchesPerCandidate: 22, and it is the CAP the floor of 20 requires rather than a number with its own anchor — the same cap-minus-floor relation stage2_entry.maxLaunchesPerCandidate holds at 10-against-8, kept at TWO for the same reason and re-derived here in credits instead of requests. WHAT THE GAP BUYS is unchanged and captain decision 190a owns the argument: the cap is how many launches Stage 2 PLANS, the floor is how many it must SCORE, so the difference is how many planned launches a candidate may LOSE and still reach a verdict at all. At 22 against 20 it absorbs TWO, exactly as it does on the swap-api source. WHAT IT COSTS HERE: windows scanned is the lever, so this cap sets the per-candidate scan directly — 22 windows a candidate, about 9.1 credits at the ~0.414 credits a window the block comment derives, and about 64 credits a run at maxCandidatesScored 7. TREATING CREDITS AS LINEAR IN WINDOWS IS AN APPROXIMATION AND IT ERRS HIGH, WHICH IS THE SAFE DIRECTION: a Dune execution carries a fixed floor cost that the 70-window measurement already paid for, so charging the full marginal rate to each of the 84 additional windows over-states them. The run should come in under 64 rather than over. THREE LIMITS THAT ARE NOT ARITHMETIC. Dune publishes NO price table for execution compute (see dune.worstCaseCreditsPerExecution), so ~0.414 is a per-lane pin against measured executions of ONE statement shape and not a vendor rate — a statement that grows a dex_solana.trades join is worth ~9x it with nothing else failing. The credit counter LAGS and the key is SHARED, so a sufficient balance reading is evidence and never a reservation. And none of it has run: Gate 3 has not been convened. WHY NOT WIDER, since credits plainly afford it: this cap's job is to give the floor two launches of headroom, not to buy sample size. Widening it alone buys nothing a verdict reads, because what a verdict rests on is minLaunchesSampled — and moving THAT is the entry above.

$comment: THE PRICE OF THE SEAT. Captain's standing ruling, 2026-08-02: fees are part of the entry
window, and 'enterable' means enterable AFTER what it costs to enter. Captain decision 136b
adds the field's AFTER-COST result, which is what stops the field leg being veto-only.
Keyless, and it spends NO vendor quota — it is Solana RPC, on the same host and the same
pacing as the creation walk. It spends no swap-api request either: every signature it prices
came free with a fill Stage 2 had already parsed.
IT RUNS ONLY WHEN THE FREE LEGS HAVE NOT ALREADY REFUSED. Room and the gross field are
arithmetic over fills in hand, so they are scored first; a deployer that fails either costs
zero RPC requests. That ordering is the whole cost model.
WHAT IT CANNOT SEE, and it must travel with every number this block produces: a landing tip
paid in a SEPARATE transaction of the same bundle is not recoverable from the entrant's own
transaction and is not measured anywhere in this repo's ground truth either. Its absence
biases the answer OPTIMISTICALLY — entry looks cheaper, and the field more profitable, than
either was. So the cost leg is a GATE and never a pass.

justification.maxRpcRequestsPerCandidate: 500 SINCE CAPTAIN DECISION 197b (2026-08-04), AND WHAT IT IS SIZED AGAINST IS PER-LAUNCH HEADROOM RATHER THAN A TOTAL: 500 / maxLaunchesPerCandidate 10 = 400 / 8 = 50 union transactions a launch, so captain decision 190a's launch-cap raise leaves the cost leg exactly the room it had before it. THE MEASUREMENT UNDER IT IS UNCHANGED and is still the committed tape's, re-derived 2026-08-02 rather than copied. Distinct transactions per launch, over the 235 covered launches: the create-slot scope reads p50 7, p90 13, MAX 20 (post-break p50 7, p90 12, max 14); the whole-window scope over CLOSED create-slot outsiders reads p50 18, p90 35, MAX 70 (post-break p50 19, p90 28, max 70). The two scopes are UNIONED before anything is fetched, so a closed entrant's create-slot transaction is paid for once, AND THE UNION IS WHAT MUST BE COSTED: re-running entryCostTargets as the code calls it over those 235 launches gives p50 19, p90 35, p95 41, MAX 74 distinct transactions per launch — not 7 + 18. At maxLaunchesPerCandidate 10 that is about 190 requests at the median, ~350 at p90 and ~740 at the observed worst; at the 8 this entry was first written against it read ~152 / ~280 / ~592. THE INTERACTION THAT MADE THE RAISE NECESSARY, named here because the earlier version of this entry argued only that the median and the p90 still fitted: stage2.mjs skips a WHOLE launch when the remaining per-candidate ceiling cannot cover its target list — a launch is never priced half-way — and entry.mjs then returns entry-cost-unmeasured if the priced share falls below minPricedFraction 0.8. THAT SHARE IS A HIT RATE OVER FIELD ENTRANTS, NOT OVER LAUNCHES (entry.mjs -> entryCostPriced = hitRate(field, e => Number.isFinite(e.entryCostSol))), and a launch skipped for budget is by construction one of the heaviest, so it removes a disproportionate share of the numerator while every one of its entrants stays in the denominator. TWO DIFFERENT QUANTITIES LIVE IN THIS PARAGRAPH AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME NUMBER. The first is the PER-PLANNED-LAUNCH HEADROOM, ceiling / maxLaunchesPerCandidate, which is the captain's sizing metric and is held CONSTANT by the raise at 500 / 10 = 400 / 8 = 50 requests a planned launch — that is why 500 and not another number. The second is the BREACH POINT, the sustained per-launch cost at which the priced share first falls under minPricedFraction, which on a LAUNCH-COUNT reading is ceiling / ceil(minPricedFraction x cap): 400 / ceil(0.8 x 8) = 400 / 7 = 57.1 transactions a launch at the old cap of 8, 400 / ceil(0.8 x 10) = 400 / 8 = 50.0 at the cap of 10 with the ceiling left at 400, and 500 / 8 = 62.5 at 500. So the raise does not merely restore the old 57.1, it exceeds it; an earlier version of this entry printed ~58 for both ends and understated what 500 buys. ALL THREE OF THOSE ARE UPPER BOUNDS ON THE TRUE BREACH POINT, and the direction of the approximation is known rather than guessed: minPricedFraction gates on entryCostPriced, which is hitRate(field, e => Number.isFinite(e.entryCostSol)) — a share of FIELD ENTRANTS and not of launches. A launch skipped for budget is by construction one of the heaviest, so it carries more entrants than average and takes a larger share of the numerator than the launch-count arithmetic assumes, while every one of its entrants stays in the denominator. The entrant-weighted breach point therefore bites EARLIER than 57.1 / 50.0 / 62.5, and this repository holds no measured value for it — stated as an unmeasured optimistic gap rather than filled in with an invented figure. THE MEASURED MARGINS, so the number's provenance is honest rather than asserted. Replaying entryCostTargets as the code calls it over the committed tape (235 launches, 226 ten-launch windows) under stage2.mjs's greedy skip: the 400 ceiling was NEVER reached at either cap — 0 of 226 windows skipped a single launch — and the worst ten-launch window cost 350 of 400 against the worst eight-launch window's 316, i.e. headroom 84 at a cap of 8 falling to 50 at a cap of 10. WHY 500 DESPITE THE TAPE NEVER BREACHING 400, which is the captain's reasoning and is recorded as such: that margin evidence is n = 1 deployer while a full-day run screens STRANGERS, and the observed maximum of 74 transactions on a single launch already sits above the ~50 sustained breach point a cap of 10 at 400 would have created. An unmeasured cost is never a pass, so the failure this avoids is a NULL result rather than a false positive — but it is exactly the no-verdict outcome decision 190a exists to reduce, re-introduced on the busiest and therefore most gate-relevant candidates. An earlier version of this entry printed 200 / 380 / 700, which is the same arithmetic with the union left out (the plain sums 25 / 48 / 90 x 8); it overstated the cost by ~30% and the conclusion survives under either reading. The ceiling covers the median and the p90 whole and truncates only a pathological candidate, and it truncates VISIBLY: a launch is never priced half-way, so the ceiling costs whole launches and entry.coverage.cost records how many. THE NEW COST, stated here rather than discovered later: at the pinned 2.5s that is about 8 minutes per candidate at the median (190 requests at the cap of 10; it was ~6 at 152 requests under the cap of 8, and the ~8 an earlier version printed was the un-unioned 200) and about 21 at the ceiling, and at the maxCandidatesScored of 7 pinned on 2026-08-04 the declared worst case is 7 x 500 = 3,500 RPC requests and about 146 minutes (it read 3 x 500 = 1,500 and about 62.5 minutes at the scoring cap of 3, against 3 x 400 = 1,200 and about 50 minutes before this ceiling moved). The dry run prints it. The realistic cost is far lower because only candidates that survive room AND the gross field are priced at all — at the scoring cap of 3 the committed live run had one such candidate of three, and the same fraction at a cap of 7 is what a run actually pays.
justification.rpcMinIntervalMs: INHERITED FROM creation_walk.rpcMinIntervalMs AND NOT AN INDEPENDENT CHOICE — api.mainnet-beta rate-limits GLOBALLY across getSignaturesForAddress, getTransaction and getBlock, so this leg and the creation walk draw on one allowance. 2,500ms is that block's measured figure: 1,400ms is the documented floor but a 200-request run at that pace took over 890 seconds instead of 280 because the endpoint was shedding and the backoff was paying for it. The two legs are SERIALISED rather than run beside each other for the same reason: two concurrent jobs earned a sustained 429 lockout. Batching is not used here either — measured actively harmful on this host, 58s at batch=1 with zero shed events against 110s at batch=8 with eleven.
justification.preferBlockRoute: getBlock(slot, transactionDetails='full') returns EVERY transaction in the create slot in one request, collapsing the create-slot scope from ~7 requests a launch to 1. It is UNTESTED against this endpoint from this repo — what is known is that getBlock works here for signature listing; what is unknown is whether the public endpoint serves full blocks to this client and what a busy mainnet slot's payload costs. So it is probed BEHIND A FALLBACK: anything other than a usable block latches the candidate onto the per-signature route, and the route that ran reaches the run record so a saved run says which one paid for its numbers. It buys request count and NOTHING ELSE — in particular it does not reach out-of-transaction landing tips, because attributing a sibling transaction in the same slot to the same bundle is an inference the chain does not support. Set false to pin the walk to the proven route.

$comment: THE SCREEN GRADING ITSELF — tools/deployer-screen/grade.mjs, with prediction.mjs (what a run
claimed) and outcome.mjs (what happened). The captain's requirement, in his own words: 'we do
the same research in a repeatable way ... then loop the process continuous getting better'.
WHY THIS IS AN ACCURACY PROPERTY AND NOT A FEATURE. A run that did not record what it
predicted can NEVER be graded — not 'gradeable later', never — because neither the claim nor
the instant it stops being in-sample survives anywhere else. Every run before schema 16 is
permanently unfalsifiable. That is also this lane's scope limit: it records and grades, and it
re-tunes NOTHING. No bar here moves stage1_gate, stage2_entry or stage2_cost, and the outcome
is measured at the bars the PREDICTING run recorded rather than at today's.
THE THREE PROVIDER LEGS AND THEIR CEILINGS, all checked BEFORE the first request and refused
whole rather than half-run:
keyed MadeOnSol   1 profile per claim, maxKeyedRequests 6 (3 claims x 2 attempts)
keyless swap-api  the claim's OWN recipe, summed, against maxKeylessRequests 540
Solana RPC        the claim's OWN stage2_cost ceiling, summed, against maxRpcRequests 1500
A record whose recipe would not fit is refused with its arithmetic printed; it is never
truncated to fit, because a truncated Stage 2 walk holds the earliest entrants by slot, which
is a BIASED sample rather than a short one and would grade the screen on a sample it would
never have scored.
THE DAILY ARITHMETIC: maxKeyedRequests 6 x runsPerDayAssumed 1 = 6 of the 100,000/day
allowance, worst case — the denominator restated by captain decision 267a, which found the
MadeOnSol key is now Ultra and EXCLUSIVE to slot-zero rather than ~200/day and shared. The
feed takes up to 108 and screen.mjs takes the rest, so this lane is still deliberately the
smallest keyed consumer in the tool, by three orders of magnitude rather than by a share of a
scarce day. NOTE THE SHAPE THIS BLOCK ALREADY HAD AND budget.maxKeyedRequests HAS SINCE
ADOPTED: 6 is 3 claims x 2 ATTEMPTS, i.e. the ceiling counts the retry rather than leaving it
to headroom. It is OPERATOR-RUN, not
scheduled; putting it on a cron means raising runsPerDayAssumed here and saying what it
displaces, exactly as the feed block requires.
READING THE HIT RATE. Ungraded claims are EXCLUDED from the denominator, never counted
against the screen: every reason a claim goes ungraded is a fact about our own coverage
(captain decision 174b), so folding them in would make the screen score worse the flakier
pump.fun was that day. The ungraded tally is printed beside the rate for that reason.
STAGE 3 IS DEFERRED (captain decision 237a), so no exit claim is made or graded. The record
shape declares that absence rather than omitting it, so a later build appending an exit
subject invalidates no run committed in between.

justification.minOutcomeAgeDays: HOW LONG A CLAIM WAITS BEFORE ITS OUTCOME IS WORTH MEASURING, sized on the only launch-tempo measurement this repo holds for GATE-PASSERS specifically. runs/2026-08-02-good-vs-elite.md, 'Tempo': over the same 70-launch denominator, elite gate-passers take 26-35 days and good-tier gate-passers 34-157 days — i.e. 0.37-0.50 and 0.49-2.24 days per launch. An outcome needs stage2_entry.minLaunchesSampled 8 further launches, ALL of them after the claim's boundary, so it needs 3.0 days at the fastest measured gate-passer tempo and 17.9 at the slowest. 21 covers the slowest with ~17% headroom. NAME THE READING: that tempo is measured over the vendor's own 70-record profile page, which is the same surface the outcome walk lists launches from, so the two agree by construction; it is NOT the creation-derived history the gate reads, whose spans are far longer (median 147.1 days on the last real run's 82 candidates) and which would justify a much shorter wait for the wrong reason. THE DIRECTION OF ERROR IS DELIBERATE AND IT IS NOT SYMMETRIC: measuring too EARLY cannot produce a wrong grade — the walk reaches an unmeasured verdict, the claim stays ungraded and stays out of the denominator — but it spends a full Stage 2 walk to learn nothing, so the cost of impatience is budget. Measuring too LATE costs only latency, and the claim is not perishable. So this errs long on purpose. What would justify a different value: a measured distribution of how long a claim actually waits before its outcome first reaches a MEASURED verdict, which cannot exist until runs start carrying predictions.
justification.retryAfterDays: HOW LONG AN UNGRADED CLAIM WAITS BEFORE IT IS OFFERED AGAIN, which is what makes a rerun idempotent in the sense that matters: the same command run twice on the same day produces the same ledger and spends NOTHING the second time, while the loop still converges with no flag to remember. Sized on what a retry could possibly change: every ungraded reason is fixed only by the deployer creating more launches, so a retry before that is the same walk for the same answer. At the slowest measured gate-passer tempo above (2.24 days/launch) 14 days is ~6 further launches, which is most of the 8-launch sample a refused outcome was short of; at the fastest (0.37) it is ~38, comfortably a whole new sample. A settled grade is never retried at all — hit and miss are LATCHED by outcome.mjs -> mergeGrades, because a lane that revised its own past grades would be marking its own homework twice. What would justify a different value: the same measured waiting-time distribution minOutcomeAgeDays needs, which does not exist yet.
justification.maxClaimsPerRun: A BUDGET BOUND AND NOT A STATISTICAL ONE, the same kind of number as stage2_entry.maxCandidatesScored and stated as such. NO MEASUREMENT BACKS THE VALUE 3, because the quantity it would be sized against — how many ripe claims arrive per run — cannot be measured until runs start carrying predictions; today the committed records hold ZERO gradeable claims, which is the finding this lane exists to make visible rather than a reason to pick a bigger number. What it IS sized against is exposure, exactly: 3 x stage2_entry.maxLaunchesPerCandidate 10 x maxRequestsPerLaunch 18 = 540 = maxKeylessRequests below, so the ceiling and the declared worst case are THE SAME NUMBER and no plan-level truncation is possible — the same property that makes --dry-run the whole exposure in Stage 2 rather than a lower bound on it. Wall clock at the pinned 7s swap-api pacing is ~63 minutes for the fill walk, plus 3 x 500 = 1,500 RPC requests at 2.5s serialised on the same host (~62 minutes), so a worst-case run is ~2.1 hours. Raising it means moving maxKeylessRequests and maxRpcRequests with it or the plan stops being the exposure. What would justify a different value: a measured arrival rate of ripe claims, plus a measured share of them that reach a MEASURED outcome, once schema-16 runs exist to supply both.
justification.maxKeyedRequests: EXACT, not a margin: one GET /deployer-hunter/{wallet} per claim measured, maxClaimsPerRun 3 of them, and client.mjs -> BoundedClient retries a failed request ONCE and counts the retry against the ceiling — so 3 x 2 = 6 is the worst case and there is no seventh request this lane can issue. That profile is the only keyed call in the whole loop: the launch list, the fills and the entry cost all come from pump.fun's keyless tape and Solana's public RPC, exactly as Stage 2 does, so the shared MadeOnSol daily allowance sees 6 requests and nothing else. This lane issues NO Dune execution and NO Helius credit: it enumerates from the same vendor profile Stage 2 does, which is what makes an outcome comparable with the claim it grades rather than a reading off a different surface.
justification.maxKeylessRequests: 3 x 10 x 18 = 540 AT THE PINNED stage2_entry VALUES, and the ceiling equals the declared worst case so the dry run prints the whole exposure. THE CHECK IS AGAINST EACH CLAIM'S OWN RECORDED RECIPE, NOT AGAINST THESE PINS, and that is the load-bearing part: an outcome must be measured at the bars the predicting run applied, so a record carrying a larger maxLaunchesPerCandidate or maxRequestsPerLaunch is priced at ITS values and the run is REFUSED before its first request if the sum does not fit here. It is never scaled down to fit — stage2.mjs skips a whole launch rather than pricing one half-way for the same reason, and a truncated walk holds the earliest entrants by slot, which is a biased sample rather than a short one. It sits under budget.maxKeylessRequests, and the two legs never run at once, so this lane cannot crowd out a screen run's own walk.
justification.maxRpcRequests: 3 x stage2_cost.maxRpcRequestsPerCandidate 500 = 1,500, the run-level ceiling the per-candidate one does not provide. It exists because the per-candidate ceiling comes from the RECORD being graded rather than from this file: without a run-level bound, a record pinning a larger stage2_cost ceiling would set this lane's exposure, which is an unbounded provider call wearing a recorded number's clothes. Checked before the first request against the claims actually due, and the run is refused whole if it does not fit. Pacing is stage2_cost.rpcMinIntervalMs, inherited rather than re-pinned: api.mainnet-beta rate-limits GLOBALLY across methods, so this leg is serialised with the fill walk exactly as Stage 2's cost leg is.
justification.keylessMinIntervalMs: swap-api's own pin, mirroring stage2_entry.keylessMinIntervalMs, because this lane walks the SAME host with the SAME client and a second lane pacing it faster would shed the first lane's requests as well as its own. It is applied as max(this, the recorded run's own value) so it can only ever slow the walk down: a record written under a faster pin cannot make this lane outrun the host, and a future pin raised here cannot be undone by an old record. Pacing moves the wall clock and never the exposure — the 540 above is unchanged by it.
justification.runsPerDayAssumed: OPERATOR-RUN, ONCE A DAY AT MOST, and the number exists so the allowance arithmetic is stated rather than assumed: 6 x 1 = 6 keyed requests a day of the 100,000/day allowance (restated by captain decision 267a; it read ~200/day and shared before the key went Ultra and exclusive), against the feed's 108 and screen.mjs's remainder. It is an ASSUMPTION about how the tool is invoked and not a bound the code enforces — the enforced bound is maxKeyedRequests, per run. Putting this lane on a schedule means raising this value on purpose and saying what it displaces, which is the same rule feed.runsPerDayAssumed already states; a cron added without touching it is how a lane silently becomes the allowance's largest consumer.

$comment: THE BUNDLING CENSUS — tools/deployer-screen/bundling.mjs. Captain decision 173a (the pass) and
183a (the union re-run), 2026-08-03/04.
A WINDOWS-ONLY pass: it walks create-slot windows and reports ONLY co-ordination observables
per launch — bundledTx, runTx, maxWalletsInOneTx, adjacencyMarks, coordinatedWallets. No entry
score, no room figure, no field, no entry cost, no
verdict. It exists to SIZE a problem, not to fix one, and it moves no bar.
WHAT IT IS SIZING, AND THE PREMISE IT WAS SIZED UNDER HAS SINCE MOVED. When this pass ran,
stage2_entry pinned maxLaunchesPerCandidate 8 and minLaunchesSampled 8, deliberately equal,
and since #17 a launch whose create slot the co-ordination rule marks
nothing in is refused as unproven (measure.mjs -> roomIsProven, captain decision 134a — the
UNION since 182a, and the census CALLS that function rather than copying it). Multiplied out,
Stage 2 could only reach a verdict for a candidate whose most recent 8 eligible launches were
EVERY ONE proven. That is arithmetic. CAPTAIN DECISION 190a RAISED THE CAP TO 10 AGAINST THE
SAME FLOOR OF 8, so the live rule is now 8 proven of 10 planned and the census record's
all-of-8 headline is STRICTER than what Stage 2 requires — it understates how many candidates
are scoreable, which is the safe direction for a finding of this shape. A census record is
never retro-edited; re-running it under the new cap is a separate decision, and this block
still re-pins nothing so a re-run would measure the launches Stage 2 actually plans.
What the live evidence could not say is how large a population it
silences: the Stage 2 scoring cap is 3, so the reverification scored TWO strangers and one
control (data/slot-zero-stage2-reverify/report.md section 2a). Two of two is a signal and it is
not a rate.
NO WINDOW PARAMETER IS PINNED HERE. windowMs, seekMarginMs, windowSlotSpan, tradePageLimit,
maxLaunchesPerCandidate, maxRequestsPerLaunch and the swap-api pacing are read from
stage2_entry unchanged, because the number only means something if the census measures the
same launches Stage 2 would have refused. A second copy of any of them would let the two drift
and the finding would stop describing the tool it is about. This block pins only what is
genuinely new: how many wallets may be read and how many requests each of the two legs may
spend.
IT SPENDS NO KEYED REQUEST, and that is structural rather than careful: there is no keyed
client in bundling.mjs. The cohort comes from this repository's own committed records (the feed
ledger and every saved screen run — wallets whose keyed cost was already paid), and the launch
list comes from the KEYLESS ownership listing on frontend-api-v3.pump.fun, the same surface the
gate merges against and --consistency walks. So the MadeOnSol, Helius and Dune allowances are
untouched by it, and the bound it had to declare in advance is a zero.
THE GATE IT APPLIES IS THE OWNERSHIP READING, AND THAT READING IS BIASED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AT
ONCE, exactly as FEED.md now states. It REJECTS through the count bars — 20 of 82 wallets clear
minTokens+minSpanDays on the vendor page against 66 of 82 on the creation-derived reading — and
it INFLATES through the rate, which reads higher than the gate's on 37 of 81 wallets (lower on
29, median difference 0.0000) and by up to +0.6929 (slot-zero-gate-bar-measure-own-population
§2.1/§2.3, held in firstmate's records, not in this repo).
SO THERE IS NO SAFE DIRECTION HERE, and an earlier version of this comment claimed one. The
vendor reading is harder on the count bars and EASIER on the rate, so the surveyed population is
NEITHER A SUBSET NOR A SUPERSET of what a keyed Stage 1 would have passed — it overlaps both
ways. The disproof is in this repository: in runs/2026-08-04.json, FnW6MLyu… and DxQ1iNid… are
both vendorVerdict "gate-passed" while gate-failed on the creation-derived reading. What does
stand on its own is the COST reason, and it is why the pass does not carry the creation-derived
walk: that walk would cost ~100 keyless RPC per candidate, and not carrying it is what makes the
zero-keyed-spend bound above declarable in advance.

justification.maxCohortSize: The cohort is read off disk, so this bounds a WALL CLOCK and a shared public host, not an allowance. 120 is comfortably above what the committed records can currently offer — feed/ledger.json holds 82 wallets and the two saved runs add none the ledger does not already carry — so today it is a backstop rather than a binding cap, and it is stated as one. It exists because the ledger grows on a schedule (FEED.md: 6 runs a day, up to 6 new wallets each) while this file does not, and a census re-run in a month against an unbounded cohort would silently become a much longer job on frontend-api-v3. WHAT WOULD MOVE IT: nothing about deployers — only a decision that a bigger cohort is worth the listing requests below, which is the same trade maxListingRequests prices.
justification.maxCandidatesSurveyed: 30, the upper end of the 20-30 sample captain decision 173a asked for, and it is a BUDGET bound in exactly the sense minLaunchesSampled is one: what fixes it is the fill-request arithmetic below (30 x 10 x 18 = 5,400 = maxKeylessRequests; it read 30 x 8 x 18 = 4,320 when the pass ran, before captain decision 190a raised stage2_entry.maxLaunchesPerCandidate) and the wall clock that implies, not any statistical property of a bundling rate. NOTE WHAT THAT MEANS FOR THE HEADLINE, because the whole point of this lane is that a rate must not outrun its n: a fraction over at most 30 candidates has a granularity of 1/30 = 3.3 points and a 95% interval roughly +/-18 points at the middle of the range, so it separates 'most candidates' from 'few candidates' and settles nothing finer. The census reports its own denominator in every summary field for that reason. IT IS NOT COMPARABLE TO stage2_entry.maxCandidatesScored (3 when this pass ran, 7 since 2026-08-04) and does not touch it: that cap bounds a leg which also prices entry cost on Solana RPC and produces a verdict, and this one walks fills and reports co-ordination counts.
justification.maxListingPagesPerCandidate: 4, the same LISTING_PAGES_FOR_MERGE the screen's gate uses, so the census gates on the same depth of ownership listing the screen would have merged against rather than a shallower or deeper one. The endpoint serves 70 rows a page regardless of the limit asked for, so 4 pages is up to 280 launches — well past the 25-token gate floor and past the ~35-day/70-record vendor window the keyed profile would have offered. The listing's own ~1,050-result server ceiling and its current-creator lower bound apply whatever this value is, and are reported rather than bounded here.
justification.maxListingRequests: maxCohortSize 120 x maxListingPagesPerCandidate 4 = 480, i.e. the exact declared worst case rather than a round number above it, so the dry run's plan is the whole exposure and no plan-level truncation is possible. At budget.keylessMinIntervalMs (2,000ms, which this leg REUSES because it reaches that block's host, frontend-api-v3) that is about 16 minutes worst case. It is a separate ceiling on a separate client from the fill leg below for the reason screen.mjs gives for Stage 2's: two hosts, two pacings, and neither leg may eat the other's budget.
justification.mintTimeBackdateMs: 5,000 ms subtracted from the declared mint instant before it is handed to readLaunchWindow, so a create slot is never deleted by a clock difference between two vendors. MEASURED ON THIS ROUTE, 2026-08-03, and it is the reason this value exists rather than a copied habit: frontend-api-v3's created_timestamp carries MILLISECOND precision on older listing rows while swap-api's fill `ts` is whole seconds and floored, so the two disagree by up to two seconds and always in the direction that trips the tripwire. Probed over 6 launches of one cohort wallet: skew (created_timestamp minus oldest fill ts) 0 ms on the 3 launches whose created_timestamp ends in 000, and +1,313 / +1,813 / +2,014 ms on the 3 that carry milliseconds. readLaunchWindow compares ts < createdAtMs with ZERO slack and its own comment warns that a positive skew of one millisecond deletes an entire create slot; the first live census run measured that happening on 5 of 8 launches of the first candidate walked. 5,000 ms is 2.5x the worst skew observed here plus the 1,000 ms of shared second-granularity, and it is the SAME value tools/arrival-rate-walk/bounds.json pins as walk.mintFloorSlackMs for the same failure on a different clock pair, so this is a precedent applied rather than a number invented. WHAT IT COSTS, STATED: a genuine mint-time disagreement smaller than 5 s is no longer detected, and the seek cursor starts 5 s earlier — which cannot touch this measurement, because the create slot is the OLDEST end of the walk and the backdate only widens the walk in that direction. A token has no fill before its own create transaction, so backdating admits nothing that is not this launch's. Disagreements LARGER than 5 s still drop the launch and are still counted per run, so the tripwire is narrowed rather than disarmed. WHAT WOULD MOVE IT: a measured skew on this vendor pair above ~4 s, which this probe did not see.
justification.maxKeylessRequests: maxCandidatesSurveyed 30 x stage2_entry.maxLaunchesPerCandidate 10 x stage2_entry.maxRequestsPerLaunch 18 = 5,400 — the same construction stage2_entry.maxKeylessRequests uses (7 x 10 x 18 = 1,260), and for the same reason: the declared worst case and the ceiling are the SAME number, so the dry run prints the entire exposure and a launch is only started when a full per-launch cap of headroom remains. IT IS DERIVED, NOT CHOSEN, so it moved when the cap it reads moved: captain decision 190a took stage2_entry.maxLaunchesPerCandidate from 8 to 10 and this ceiling from 4,320 to 5,400, without this block pinning a launch cap of its own — which is exactly the property the no-re-pinning rule above exists to preserve. It is NOT bounded by budget.maxKeylessRequests, which is a per-client ceiling on the frontend-api-v3 client and constrains neither this nor Stage 2's own 1,260 (see that entry). WALL CLOCK IS WHAT THIS ACTUALLY COSTS: at stage2_entry.keylessMinIntervalMs (7,000ms, reused because it is the same host) 5,400 requests is about 10.5 hours worst case (it was 8.4 at 4,320), against an EXPECTED cost near 2.9 hours at the tape's measured p50 of 4 pages a launch plus shedding. Both figures are printed by the dry run so a slow walk is not mistaken for a hang. It spends no vendor allowance at any speed.
